title: Three-Week IB History Revision Plan for November
summary: IB History revision plan for November: use three focused weeks to triage topics, sharpen essays, complete timed papers, and protect rest.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before an IB History exam, every leader, treaty and crisis can suddenly look equally urgent. A useful **IB History revision plan** creates priorities: diagnose gaps, turn knowledge into arguments, then rehearse under timed conditions. Give each week a purpose while protecting time for other subjects.


November candidates should confirm which curriculum applies to their cohort. The current course reaches its final assessment in 2027, while the revised course begins assessment in 2028. Check your school's official timetable and guidance. For that session, RevisionDojo's[November 2026 IB History exam dates and plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-history-november-2026-exam-dates) provides a starting point.


### Your three-week checklist


Week Main priority Practice goal


Week 1 Diagnose gaps Source drills and essay plans


Week 2 Strengthen arguments Timed sections and essays


Week 3 Rehearse and consolidate Full timed papers and targeted repairs


Allow roughly 60-90 minutes on ordinary study days, adjusting around other commitments. Place longer simulations on lighter days and keep one evening free each week.


### Week 1: Diagnose your IB History revision gaps


Before rereading, test what you can retrieve. Choose a representative question and spend five minutes planning an answer without notes. Assess each topic using three labels:


- **Green:** clear chronology, precise evidence and a defensible argument.
- **Amber:** familiar material, but unreliable recall or weak connections to the question.
- **Red:** unclear chronology, missing evidence or uncertain central debates.


A plan containing only “economic problems caused instability” needs work. Stronger knowledge supplies policies, dates, comparisons and qualifications that explain the claim.


Prioritise red and amber topics relevant to your papers. Reconstruct weak material using a short chronology and an evidence sheet, then close your notes and retrieve it again. Maintain green topics through brief checks using[IB History Flashcards and Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-ib-history-coverage) .


For Paper 1, practise explaining a source's message and analysing its value and limitations with reference to origin, purpose and content. The guide to[IB History Paper 1 and Paper 2 strategies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-ace-ib-history-paper-1-and-paper-2-exams-proven-tips-free-resources) helps distinguish source analysis from essay writing.


Across the week, alternate knowledge repair with source exercises and essay plans. End with a mixed diagnostic session to check whether your weakest areas have improved.


Two students compare an enormous revision pile with a crowded exam timetable


### Week 2: Turn knowledge into arguments


Knowing what happened is only the beginning. Your answer must explain significance, address the command term and sustain a judgement.


Build a compact argument sheet for each major topic. Include recurring themes, contrasting interpretations, precise evidence and useful comparisons. Practise adapting this material to different questions. A question about the importance of economic conditions requires a different judgement from one asking you to compare methods of political control.


Use the[RevisionDojo IB History Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-history/questionbank) to target weaker topics. Start with plans and individual paragraphs, then attempt complete timed essays. AI Chat can help unpack an unclear concept, while grading tools can suggest areas to review. Check feedback against your course criteria and teacher guidance before revising your response.


Keep an error log that distinguishes four problems:


- **Knowledge:** missing or inaccurate evidence.
- **Reasoning:** evidence listed without explanation or judgement.
- **Structure:** paragraphs that drift from the question.
- **Timing:** sections that consume disproportionate time.


Match the repair to the problem. A forgotten date needs retrieval; an unsupported judgement needs better reasoning. Record the correction and test it in your next attempt.


The guide to[IB History essay structure](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-history-essay-structure-7-worthy-response) explains how claims, evidence, analysis and qualification work together. At HL, reserve a substantial practice block for Paper 3 rather than fitting it around other papers.


### Week 3: Rehearse the November exam


Complete at least one realistic timed session for each paper you will sit. Match the official duration and permitted materials, and stop when time expires. Use Exam mode for timed practice; Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can provide unfamiliar questions for additional rehearsal.


Review the decisions behind the result. Did your thesis answer the exact question? Did each paragraph advance it? Was your evidence precise? Did comparison continue throughout an answer that required it? Identify where time disappeared.


Follow each simulation with a focused repair. Rewrite a weak introduction, rebuild an essay plan or repeat a source exercise. Complete that correction before starting another full paper. Otherwise, repeated practice can simply reproduce the same weakness.


For recurring difficulties, consult the[comprehensive IB History exam preparation guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/comprehensive-guide-to-preparing-for-the-ib-history-exam) . Students working independently can also use these[IB History self-study resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-history-resources-self-study) , or seek targeted feedback from RevisionDojo Tutors.


Aim to finish your last substantial simulation around three days before the exam. Then review your error log, core evidence and selected plans. Keep the final day light, confirm practical arrangements and protect sleep. Adjust this sequence around other examinations rather than forcing a rigid schedule.


### Keep the plan workable across subjects


At the start of each week, mark fixed commitments and other examinations. Place demanding History work where you have enough energy, then use shorter gaps for chronology checks, Flashcards or essay plans.


If another subject becomes urgent, preserve retrieval and targeted practice. Reduce passive rereading first. A focused 35-minute session can still produce a useful plan and a corrected mistake.


RevisionDojo brings the process together through its Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams and Tutors. The Coursework Library supports coursework needs; during exam revision, choose resources that address the weakness in front of you.


Three weeks becomes manageable when every session has a clear job. Diagnose first, strengthen arguments next, then rehearse. Begin with one question in the Questionbank and let the evidence from your answer determine tomorrow's work.
